open_points.subject: A05 edge order and flow-version identity
open_points.text: edges, by (`to_node`, `to_port`, `from_node`, `from_port`); Lists whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ... edges in the edge order of A05
open_points.question: How are two edges with the same endpoints but different guards ordered for first-failure reporting and canonical identity?
options: Add the guard port and guard value as tie-breakers
Preserve submission order for tied edges
Refuse all edges whose endpoint tuples repeat
open_points.default_guess: Order tied edges by the canonical JSON of their guards.

open_points.subject: A05/A01 constant order and flow-version identity
open_points.text: constants, by (`to_node`, `to_port`); a port with a constant has no other constant
open_points.question: How are multiple constants targeting the same port ordered before the proof rejects them and before the flow version is hashed?
options: Add the constant's canonical value and class as tie-breakers
Preserve submission order for tied constants
Reject duplicate targets before computing an identity
open_points.default_guess: Reject duplicate constant targets as malformed composition before hashing.

open_points.subject: A04 authored trial-case inputs
open_points.text: it is added only when its input values fit the contract version's input ports
open_points.question: Must a trial case supply exactly every input port and no unknown ports, or may inputs be missing or extra?
options: Require exactly the contract's input ports
Allow omitted inputs
Ignore or retain unknown extra inputs
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly one value for every input port and no extras.

open_points.subject: A04 trial-case expected outputs
open_points.text: its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports; if the case states expected outputs, every output's digest equals the expected one
open_points.question: When `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every output port, or may it specify only a subset?
options: Require every output and no extras
Compare only the outputs supplied by the case
Allow missing outputs but reject extras
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly every output port and no extras.

open_points.subject: A04 rollback eligibility
open_points.text: Rollback activates an earlier implementation of the slot's current contract version
open_points.question: What makes an implementation “earlier”: submission order, activation order, or merely being different from the current implementation, and may a later previously activated implementation be selected after rolling back?
options: Earlier by implementation submission order only
Earlier by activation history
Any non-current implementation with a current-corpus admitted verdict
open_points.default_guess: Allow any implementation of the current contract version that has an admitted verdict over the current corpus.

open_points.subject: A04 admitted verdict and automatic activation
open_points.text: An `admitted` verdict is followed at once, in the same request, by an Activation M09 by the kernel
open_points.question: Must writing the admitted verdict and its automatic activation be one atomic store transaction, and what state is recovered if the process stops between them?
options: Write verdict and activation atomically
Permit a persisted verdict without activation and activate it on restart
Permit the gap until the implementation is submitted again
open_points.default_guess: Write the verdict and activation in the same store transaction.

open_points.subject: Admission evidence across kernel releases
open_points.text: an AdmissionVerdict M08 for that implementation and the current corpus digest already exists, in which case that verdict is used; A release pins the exact versions of ... the sandbox runtime
open_points.question: After an upgrade changes the Python runtime or sandbox dependencies, do existing admission verdicts remain valid even though the same implementation may execute differently?
options: Keep all existing verdicts valid
Include the release/runtime identity in admission validity
Require re-admission after a runtime-changing release
open_points.default_guess: Require a new admission verdict when the sandbox runtime identity changes.

open_points.subject: Runs recovered after a release change
open_points.text: a function element without a concluded record is executed again; the sandbox interpreter of release v1 is CPython 3.12
open_points.question: Does a run pin its sandbox release, or may restart recovery execute its pinned implementation under a newer runtime than the one under which the run started?
options: Runs pin and require their original sandbox release
Recovery uses the currently installed release
Runs crossing an incompatible release fail
open_points.default_guess: Recovery uses the current release only if its sandbox runtime identity matches the run's pinned release.

open_points.subject: A20 lowered non-contract ceilings
open_points.text: A new release may change ceilings. They bind contract versions issued after it; a contract version issued earlier keeps its bounds
open_points.question: What happens to existing trial fixtures, stored values, pending run spools, requests and service responses that exceed a newly lowered global ceiling not stored in a contract version?
options: Grandfather every existing artifact and pending run
Apply new ceilings whenever an artifact is next read or used
Refuse startup if retained artifacts exceed the new ceilings
open_points.default_guess: Grandfather already stored artifacts and runs, while applying new ceilings to newly received data.

open_points.subject: K-02 and A03 filesystem access
open_points.text: no filesystem beyond its input; No host directory is mounted except the read-only runtime and that exchange directory; opening any path outside the exchange directory and the read-only runtime [raises]
open_points.question: May agent code read runtime files and freely read or write the exchange directory, or must filesystem access be restricted to the supplied input and runner-managed output only?
options: Permit user code to access the runtime and exchange directory
Permit imports but deny user-initiated runtime-file reads and restrict exchange paths
Treat any filesystem access by user code as a sandbox violation
open_points.default_guess: Permit runner-managed input/output and imports, but reject other user-initiated filesystem access.

open_points.subject: A03 clock and randomness prohibition
open_points.text: replaces every clock and randomness entry point ... The replaced entry points are exactly: ... The list is closed for the release; an entry point found missing is added by a new release
open_points.question: What is the outcome when code obtains time or randomness through a standard-library entry point not in the frozen trap list?
options: It is permitted until a later release adds a trap
It must still be detected as `sandbox_violation`
The release must refuse to start unless it proves the list exhaustive
open_points.default_guess: Treat any detected clock or randomness access as `sandbox_violation` and require the release test to establish coverage.

open_points.subject: Pure-function determinism
open_points.text: A function node runs one admitted implementation ... no clock, no randomness; The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice
open_points.question: Is referentially deterministic output a required invariant for every implementation, and if so how are other Python runtime observables that can vary between executions prevented or detected?
options: Purity means only no external effects; differing outputs are allowed
Every execution must be deterministic and nondeterminism is a sandbox violation
Determinism is tested only by the trial corpus without a general guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Treat purity as no external effects and require deterministic admission evidence, without claiming all Python nondeterminism can be prevented.

open_points.subject: A03 outcome classification for OS-enforced limits
open_points.text: a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`; the process exited abnormally — `crashed`
open_points.question: How does the kernel distinguish an abnormal exit caused by an enforced memory or process limit from an unrelated crash when both conditions appear true?
options: Observable limit enforcement always takes precedence as `resource_exhausted`
Any unattributed signal or exit is `crashed`
Define exact signals, exit codes and accounting evidence for each limit
open_points.default_guess: Classify as `resource_exhausted` only when the parent can attribute the termination to a specific enforced limit; otherwise use `crashed`.

open_points.subject: Many-file list disclosure class
open_points.text: the reference naming the list carries the list's class, so an empty one keeps it; M23 inputs, outputs: references ... to SpooledFiles by their facts, by port
open_points.question: Where is the disclosure class of a many-file list stored, especially for an empty list that has no SpooledFile record from which a class can be derived?
options: Add a persisted list-reference record carrying the class
Store a per-port list class in NodeExecution inputs and outputs
Derive the class from context and never persist it
open_points.default_guess: Persist the list's class with the per-port file-list reference in each relevant execution record.

open_points.subject: Mapped-element retries
open_points.text: a concluded element is never executed again; Resume ... sends again ... every element waiting on `service_unreachable`; `not_applied` ... the next send ... is the next attempt
open_points.question: Does “concluded element” mean any element with a NodeExecution, or only an element whose overall conclusion is final rather than a retryable wait?
options: Never retry an element after any NodeExecution
Retry elements whose latest record represents `service_unreachable` or resolved `not_applied`
Create a new logical element for each retry
open_points.default_guess: Treat only a final element conclusion as concluded; retryable attempts may produce later NodeExecutions for the same element.

open_points.subject: Manifest record validation
open_points.text: the service record is absent, is not valid JSON, lacks `service` or `capabilities`, or its `service` field differs; one entry of the record's `capabilities`
open_points.question: How are wrong JSON types, duplicate object member names, malformed capability entries, and malformed instance or required-header containers classified and ordered when the listed fields exist but do not have the assumed shapes?
options: Treat every malformed shape as the corresponding manifest-mismatch check
Treat unsupported shapes as an internal error
Defer all exact manifest schemas and their failure order to a later state
open_points.default_guess: Treat every structural or type error as a manifest mismatch, ordered at the field where it is first read.

open_points.subject: Service `api_base_url`
open_points.text: an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host; The URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path
open_points.question: Are user information, query strings, fragments, non-root path prefixes, repeated trailing slashes, IPv6 zone identifiers and other valid absolute-URL components allowed, and exactly how are they joined and represented in the `Host` header?
options: Allow every absolute HTTP URL and define component-aware joining
Restrict the base URL to scheme, authority and an optional path prefix
Restrict it to scheme and authority only
open_points.default_guess: Restrict `api_base_url` to an HTTP(S) scheme and authority with an optional normalized path prefix, and forbid user information, query and fragment.

open_points.subject: Plain-HTTP loopback exception
open_points.text: one whose `api_base_url` host is a loopback address
open_points.question: Is loopback determined from the literal host syntax, DNS resolution, every resolved address, or the address actually connected to, and do names such as `localhost` qualify?
options: Only literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback addresses qualify
Resolve the name and require every result to be loopback
Use the actual connected address
open_points.default_guess: Allow plain HTTP only when the URL contains a literal loopback IP address.

open_points.subject: Path-placeholder encoding
open_points.text: Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.
open_points.question: Which characters remain unescaped, what hex-letter case is used, how integers are converted to text, and how an existing percent sign or Unicode string is encoded?
options: Use the exact RFC 3986 unreserved set and uppercase UTF-8 percent escapes
Use an HTTP library's path-segment encoder
Encode every byte
open_points.default_guess: Use UTF-8, leave only RFC 3986 unreserved bytes unescaped, and emit uppercase percent escapes.

open_points.subject: JSON request body
open_points.text: for `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` they form one JSON object body keyed by port name; with a body, `content-type` and `content-length`
open_points.question: What exact JSON byte serialization and `Content-Type` value are used for a non-multipart request body?
options: RFC 8785 canonical JSON with `application/json`
A fixed compact JSON encoding distinct from JCS
Implementation-library JSON encoding
open_points.default_guess: Use RFC 8785 canonical JSON bytes and `Content-Type: application/json`.

open_points.subject: Multipart request and exact approval
open_points.text: the fully built request as the owner was shown it — method, URL, headers and body. Any difference at send ... asks again; the `multipart/form-data` content type without its `boundary` parameter; the boundary is not part of it
open_points.question: Does approval cover the exact multipart bytes and boundary sent on the wire, or only the abstract ordered parts?
options: Include the chosen boundary and exact encoded body bytes in the approved request
Approve only the abstract parts and permit any conforming boundary and encoding
Choose one release-fixed boundary algorithm so the abstract description determines the bytes
open_points.default_guess: Use a deterministic multipart serialization and include its resulting body digest and content type in the approved request.

open_points.subject: Multipart part-name safety
open_points.text: `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with `filename="<port>"` added for a file part; every port name is unique within its direction
open_points.question: How are quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII text and other characters in a port name escaped or refused when inserted into multipart header parameters?
options: Restrict multipart-used port names to a safe ASCII token grammar
Define quoted-string escaping and an encoding for non-ASCII names
Insert names verbatim
open_points.default_guess: Refuse a binding with multipart-used port names outside a defined safe ASCII field-name grammar.

open_points.subject: Partial HTTP responses
open_points.text: request may have been sent, no valid final response received (timeout, reset, EOF ...); status 2xx, outputs do not fit rule 3
open_points.question: If a valid 2xx, 4xx, 5xx or 3xx status and headers arrive but the body then times out, resets or ends prematurely, does the status row decide the outcome or does the earlier “no valid final response” row win?
options: Any incomplete body uses the no-valid-response row
A received final status decides effect application, with body failures handled under that status
Status decides only for responses whose complete body was received
open_points.default_guess: Once a valid final status is received, use that status's row; for 2xx, an incomplete body is a contract violation and a non-read attempt is `applied`.

open_points.subject: A16 token-list reread after invalid configuration
open_points.text: compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read; when they differ ... it re-reads it; When any fails, every request is refused ... until a re-read passes
open_points.question: After a changed file is readable but fails parsing or token validation, is its digest recorded as the “last read” digest, and how is the same unchanged file retried on later requests?
options: Keep the last valid digest so every request retries the invalid file
Record the invalid digest but force a reread while configuration is invalid
Record the invalid digest and retry only after another byte change
open_points.default_guess: Track an invalid configuration state and force a full reread on every request until validation succeeds.

open_points.subject: Global startup checks
open_points.text: The kernel checks at start, before recovery ... that `bubblewrap` is present; the installation refuses to start ...; a second process ... refuses to start; the kernel refuses to start otherwise
open_points.question: What is the fixed order of configuration, token, credential-header collision, data-directory, lock, manifest-dependent, sandbox-probe and recovery checks when several would fail, and which failure is reported first?
options: Define one global startup-check order
Allow implementation-dependent first failure
Run independent checks and return a fixed ordered collection of failures
open_points.default_guess: Define a single global startup order beginning with configuration and filesystem safety, then the exclusive lock, release/sandbox checks, manifest-dependent checks, and finally recovery.
